basis: Complete lyric movements marked by address, invitation, question-answer, search/find sequence, descriptive praise catalogue, setting and imagery shift, repeated adjuration, procession, garden/vineyard movement, family exchange, and closing reciprocal calls. Canonical relations, grammatical gender/number, supplied speaker labels, Hebrew or Greek evidence, and later reception remain evidence only.
proposal_bias: Prefer the larger coherent poem, exchange, search scene, praise catalogue, invitation, or refrain-governed movement. Preserve exact larger alternatives and lower confidence wherever a seam depends on speaker identity, dramatic reconstruction, gender assignment, translation, versification, or interpretive priority.

chunks.marker: A compact relation formula names the song before the first-person desire speech begins at 1:2.
chunks.rejection: The formula may be read in more than one way and does not settle attribution; the explicit discourse shift at 1:2 supports retaining it as a title while preserving title-plus-opening alternatives.
chunks.risk: Turning the relation to Solomon into authorship, chronology, historical speaker identity, royal marriage reconstruction, or theology.
chunks.hold: defer Hebrew relation-formula translation, title function, authorship, chronology, and historical attribution

chunks.form: opening desire, self-description, and location exchange
chunks.marker: First-person desire and fragrance/name language moves through address to Jerusalem's daughters, vineyard/self-description, and a where-do-you-pasture question answered by a flock-path response.
chunks.rejection: Supplied English speaker headings and gender assignments cannot create seams; the complete opening movement is retained through its question-answer closure.
chunks.risk: Overconfident speaker count, gender identity, court scene, social-status reconstruction, complexion interpretation, or sanitization of desire.
chunks.hold: defer speakers, addressees, gender/number shifts, 1:4 and 1:7-8 voice allocation, and social-historical reconstruction

chunks.form: reciprocal praise and presence exchange closed by adjuration
chunks.marker: Praise comparisons, ornaments, perfume, dwelling and flora imagery, mutual beauty speech, and embrace language culminate in the first daughters-of-Jerusalem adjuration at 2:7.
chunks.rejection: Speaker alternation is internal to a reciprocal lyric movement, and the adjuration supplies the stronger closure; no individual famous image is isolated.
chunks.risk: Using speaker headings to atomize the exchange, treating metaphor as biography, imposing marriage chronology, or letting later allegorical, Marian, ecclesial, or Christological readings dictate seams.
chunks.hold: defer exact voice allocation, 2:1-2 comparison roles, adjuration wording, erotic/marital reconstruction, and reception priority

chunks.form: arrival and spring invitation poem with closing reciprocal call
chunks.marker: An approaching beloved is announced; rise-and-come imperatives are grounded in seasonal renewal, followed by concealment, vineyard protection, mutual belonging, and an until-day-breathes closing call.
chunks.rejection: The foxes and mutual-belonging lines remain within the invitation's imagery and response horizon; the scene is not divided to privilege a literal, allegorical, or moral reading.
chunks.risk: Famous-verse extraction, zoological or sexual euphemism certainty, forced dramatic staging, marriage sequence, or messianic/revival interpretation.
chunks.hold: defer speaker assignment, 2:15 attachment, fox/vineyard referents, 2:17 translation, setting, plot, and theological reception

chunks.form: nocturnal search, encounter, finding, and adjuration scene
chunks.marker: Repeated seeking without finding leads through city and watchmen encounter to finding and holding, then closes with the repeated daughters-of-Jerusalem adjuration.
chunks.rejection: Search, encounter, and adjuration form one movement; whether the sequence is dream, memory, drama, or lyric convention is not decided by the boundary.
chunks.risk: Treating the scene as a continuous historical plot, moralizing the watchmen, reconstructing a wedding timeline, or isolating the adjuration.
chunks.hold: defer genre of experience, speaker identity, house/mother setting, historicity, and plot chronology

chunks.marker: A new 'who is this coming up' question opens a scented wilderness procession; litter, warriors, carriage, daughters, king, crown, and wedding-day language culminate in a public beholding call.
chunks.rejection: The catalogue remains under the procession's governing question, but royal naming does not identify every speaker or make the whole book a historical wedding drama.
chunks.risk: Solomonic authorship/historicity inference, forced royal wedding chronology, allegorical procession theology, or sanitizing the sensory display.
chunks.hold: defer 3:6 speaker and gender, litter/carriage terminology, historical referents, composition date, and royal-wedding reconstruction

chunks.marker: A beauty declaration governs a sustained head-to-breasts comparison series and closes with the summary that the praised figure is wholly beautiful and without blemish.
chunks.rejection: Body parts and metaphors are list elements, not independent chunks; 4:6's until-day-breathes formula remains within the praise closure while its relation to 4:8 is preserved as disputed.
chunks.risk: Anatomical atomization, gender or beauty ontology, sanitization, objectification harmonization, or treating 4:7 as a doctrinal statement.
chunks.hold: defer 4:6 attachment, metaphor referents, gendered ideals, ethics, and later ecclesial or Marian reception

chunks.form: invitation, enclosed-garden praise, and garden response
chunks.marker: Come-with-me and heart-capturing address develops into sister/bride, fragrance, spring, garden, and spices imagery; a garden invitation receives an entry/eating response across the chapter seam.
chunks.rejection: The invitation and response belong together across the chapter boundary, but their exact voices and marital or sexual setting are not settled.
chunks.risk: Chapter fallback, supplied-speaker dependence, erotic-imagery sanitization, marriage consummation certainty, geographical historicism, or allegorical garden theology.
chunks.hold: defer speakers at 4:16 and 5:1, relationship status, scene, sexual/marital reconstruction, place-name force, and theological interpretation

chunks.form: extended night encounter, loss-search, watchmen wound, daughters exchange, praise catalogue, and mutual-belonging answer
chunks.marker: A sleeping-yet-awake opening leads through delayed response, disappearance, city search and watchmen violence; an adjuration prompts the daughters' question, a complete descriptive praise answer, a second question, and the garden/mutual-belonging response.
chunks.rejection: The daughters' questions bind search, praise, and location answer into a larger exchange; the watchmen episode is not minimized, allegorized away, or used to impose a single plot.
chunks.risk: Sanitizing or spiritualizing violence, blaming the seeker, forcing dream/drama chronology, isolating the famous praise catalogue, or assigning every voice by English headings.
chunks.hold: defer dream/scene status, voice allocation, 5:6 syntax, watchmen interpretation, violence and ethics, gendered praise, and 6:2-3 imagery

chunks.form: renewed beauty praise and singularity/army catalogue
chunks.marker: A fresh beauty comparison opens; eyes, hair and teeth resume earlier praise, then queens, concubines, maidens, mother, daughters, and an awe-filled 'who is this' recognition culminate the unit.
chunks.rejection: The catalogue and singularity contrast remain one praise movement; royal-harem language neither proves a historical court nor defines the relationship.
chunks.risk: Harem biography, Solomonic chronology, gender hierarchy, military-erotic sanitization, or later community allegory controlling the seam.
chunks.hold: defer speaker, historical setting, queen/concubine numbers and referents, 6:10 voice, and theological reception

chunks.form: garden descent, sudden transport or desire statement, and return-call exchange
chunks.marker: A garden inspection begins, followed by an exceptionally difficult sudden movement at 6:12 and repeated return imperatives with a closing question at 6:13.
chunks.rejection: The difficult syntax and voice allocation make smaller seams unsafe; retain the full transition LOW without selecting a translation of 6:12 or identifying the named/addressee figure in 6:13.
chunks.risk: Translation choice becoming boundary authority, invented chariot scene, proper-name certainty, dance reconstruction, gender overconfidence, or forced drama.
chunks.hold: frontier defer 6:12 syntax and lexemes, 6:13 naming/versification/speaker/addressee, scene transition, and relation to 7:1

chunks.form: dance-addressed or renewed descriptive body-praise catalogue
chunks.marker: A foot-to-head descriptive sequence proceeds through paired body imagery, stature and fruit clusters, then shifts into first-person resolve to climb and enjoy before the speech trails into the next response.
chunks.rejection: The body catalogue is kept intact rather than split by metaphor or presumed chorus/lover headings; the 7:9/7:10 speech seam is translation- and voice-sensitive.
chunks.risk: Supplied heading dependence, dance or wedding staging, anatomical atomization, erotic sanitization, gender ontology, and WEB/MT numbering confusion.
chunks.hold: defer 6:13/7:1 versification relation, speaker count, 7:9 speech transition, metaphor translation, scene, and ethics

chunks.form: mutual-belonging response, countryside invitation, public-kinship wish, embrace, and adjuration
chunks.marker: A mutual-belonging declaration leads to come-and-go countryside imperatives and stored-fruit imagery; the chapter seam continues into a kinship wish and embrace, closing with the third daughters-of-Jerusalem adjuration.
chunks.rejection: The invitation and adjuration frame a cross-chapter movement; the sibling wish is lyric comparison, not authority for biography, incest claims, marriage status, or social law.
chunks.risk: Chapter fallback, famous belonging-verse isolation, literalizing kinship imagery, reconstructing public/private marriage customs, or using 8:4 to settle desire ethics.
chunks.hold: defer speakers, kinship metaphor, social setting, relationship status, mandrake/fruit imagery, adjuration translation, and ethical/theological rulings

chunks.form: wilderness emergence question and love-seal poem
chunks.marker: A new 'who is this coming up' question and awakening/birth setting lead into seal imperatives, love/death and jealousy/grave comparisons, flame and waters, and the cannot-be-bought closure.
chunks.rejection: The famous love-seal lines stay with their emergence/awakening frame, but the unit does not define one exhaustive theology, marriage doctrine, or divine-name reading.
chunks.risk: Famous-verse isolation, marriage-proof-texting, death/resurrection or messianic imposition, preferred translation of the flame expression, and suppression of jealousy or erotic force.
chunks.hold: defer 8:5 speakers and birth imagery, 8:6 divine-name or intensive reading, love/jealousy semantics, ethics, and later theological reception

chunks.form: younger-sister problem, wall-or-door alternatives, and first-person maturity response
chunks.marker: A plural deliberative question about a little sister receives conditional wall/door plans, followed by a first-person 'I am a wall' answer and peace/favor result.
chunks.rejection: The problem, proposed alternatives, and answer belong together; they cannot securely reconstruct guardians, age, marriage negotiation, sexual status, or social ethics.
chunks.risk: Patriarchal or emancipatory system selection from ambiguous imagery, speaker/gender certainty, biography, and sanitization or oversexualization.
chunks.hold: defer speakers, sister identity, wall/door and breasts imagery, maturity/sexual-status claims, ancient social practice, and ethics

chunks.marker: A named vineyard, keepers, and thousand-silver account is answered by a first-person 'my vineyard is before me' statement allocating the thousand and two hundred.
chunks.rejection: The paired vineyard account is retained as a compact saying/exchange; naming Solomon does not settle authorship, date, historical economics, speaker, or ideological evaluation.
chunks.risk: Autobiographical Solomonic reading, royal-economic reconstruction, anti-royal or pro-royal theology, dowry/price certainty, and collapsing vineyard imagery across the book.
chunks.hold: defer speakers, ownership and payment syntax, historical referent, economic practice, authorship, chronology, and political theology

chunks.form: final reciprocal hearing and haste calls
chunks.marker: An address to one dwelling in gardens asks to hear the voice; the answer calls the beloved to flee or hasten like a gazelle/deer on spice mountains, closing the collection.
chunks.rejection: The paired calls form the larger close; supplied speaker labels, eschatological reuse, or a presumed dramatic resolution cannot force a smaller seam.
chunks.risk: Ending-theology smuggling, messianic or eschatological identification, forced reunion/departure plot, and speaker/gender overconfidence.
chunks.hold: defer speakers, force of flee/hasten, relation to earlier gazelle/mountain refrains, dramatic outcome, and later canonical reception

premortem_holds.risk: Supplied English speaker headings or grammatical gender/number are converted into a fixed cast, continuous drama, historical plot, or marriage chronology.
premortem_holds.appeal: Treat voice shifts as local discourse evidence only; preserve larger exchanges and route every identity, cast, plot, and chronology claim to Hebrew lyric and historical specialists.

premortem_holds.risk: A literal, allegorical, typological, messianic, Christological, ecclesial, Marian, ethical, or marriage reading is made boundary authority.
premortem_holds.appeal: Record reception and canonical relations separately; no interpretive priority, theology, or ethical system may create, remove, or promote a seam.

premortem_holds.risk: Erotic imagery is sanitized, atomized, spiritualized away, or used to overstate precise anatomy, sexual acts, relationship status, or consent history.
premortem_holds.appeal: Keep complete praise, invitation, garden, search, and love-poem movements; route lexicon, imagery, ancient love poetry, gender, and ethics externally without deciding them.

premortem_holds.risk: The three adjurations or famous belonging lines are detached as slogans, or their translation is harmonized to force one refrain scheme.
premortem_holds.appeal: Attach each adjuration to the larger movement it closes, retain exact wider alternatives, and defer gazelle/hind, divine-host, desire-awakening, and refrain-identity questions.

premortem_holds.risk: The cross-chapter garden response and extended night-search/daughters exchange are broken at chapter boundaries or forced into a single wedding-night plot.
premortem_holds.appeal: Preserve Song.4.8-Song.5.1 and Song.5.2-Song.6.3 as exact larger movements while deferring voices, dream/scene, relationship status, violence, and chronology.

premortem_holds.risk: The most difficult syntax, proper-name possibilities, dance term, supplied heading, or WEB/MT numbering seam is silently resolved into a scene and speaker map.
premortem_holds.appeal: Keep Song.6.11-Song.6.13 and Song.7.1-Song.7.9 LOW, preserve the exact joined alternative Song.6.11-Song.7.9, and require Hebrew/textual plus translation review.

premortem_holds.risk: The love-seal poem is isolated from its frame or made an exhaustive doctrine of marriage, God, death, resurrection, jealousy, or economics.
premortem_holds.appeal: Retain 8:5-7 as one LOW poem, preserve 8:6-7 as an exact alternative, and defer the flame expression, speaker allocation, theology, and ethics.

premortem_holds.risk: Ambiguous family and vineyard sayings are converted into a biography, guardianship/marriage custom, sexual-status ruling, royal economy, Solomonic authorship, or final dramatic resolution.
premortem_holds.appeal: Keep the family exchange, vineyard account, and reciprocal close distinct but LOW; preserve larger alternatives and route social history, Hebrew syntax, authorship, and reception externally.
